title: Three-Fruit Marmalade
subtitle: Orange, lemon, and grapefruit marmalade, sharp, well-balanced, good all year
excerpt: Three-fruit marmalade uses sweet orange, lemon, and grapefruit together, giving a sharp, balanced preserve that doesn't need the brief Seville season. Makes about six 450 g jars.
sourceNotes: Mrs Beeton (PG #10136); Pam Corbin, Preserves. The three-fruit combination provides year-round pectin and bitterness without relying on Seville oranges.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Prepare and soak the peel the night before.

glossaryTerms.definition: 105 °C for marmalade. Confirmed by the wrinkle test on a chilled plate.

content.text: Three-fruit marmalade can be made any time of year because it uses fruits that are always available,  sweet orange, lemon, and grapefruit. The grapefruit provides the bitterness, the lemon adds sharpness and pectin, and the orange brings body and sweetness. Makes about six 450 g jars.

Halve and juice all the fruit. Reserve the juice. Scrape all the pips and pith from the halved skins into a muslin square and tie tightly. Shred the peel,  fine, medium, or thick to your preference. Grapefruit peel benefits from finer shredding as it can be tough if cut thick. Put peel, muslin bundle, juice, and water in the jam pan.

Bring to a simmer and cook gently with the lid on for 1½ to 2 hours until the peel is completely soft. Press a piece between your fingers,  it should collapse without resistance. This step cannot be rushed.
Add sugar and boil to setting point
Remove and squeeze the muslin bundle into the pan. Add the sugar and stir over low heat until dissolved. Bring to a full hard boil. Cook until 105 (the
) °C, about 15 to 20 minutes. Test on a cold plate. When the surface wrinkles, take off the heat, skim, rest 10 minutes, stir, then jar and seal.

items.cause: Grapefruit peel takes longer to soften than orange or lemon.
items.fix: Simmer for at least 2 hours, or soak overnight in the water before cooking.

items.cause: Too much grapefruit relative to orange.
items.fix: Adjust to 300 g grapefruit, 600 g orange, 300 g lemon for a milder batch.

items.cause: Jarred at too high a temperature before the marmalade began to thicken.
items.fix: Rest 10 minutes and stir gently before ladling.

items.cause: Muslin bundle not squeezed enough, pectin was left behind.
items.fix: Squeeze firmly until the muslin feels almost dry, then return the squeeze to the pan. The pectin is in that liquid.
